title: What is known about 1RB0LD_1RC1RE_1LA0RA_1LE1LC_1RF1RC_---1RA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LD_1RC1RE_1LA0RA_1LE1LC_1RF1RC_---1RA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The run is a walker and carry machine whose carries apply a 5/4 map to the length of the tail, a Collatz-like rule. The walker sweeps, the shallow carries and their step counts are exact (Lean proves the walker sweeps for all lengths); the deeper carries are run cell by cell. No halt in the first 3.2·1012 steps (the run stopped inside a deep event with a tail of 853,485 groups).

claims.title: The walker, for all lengths
claims.text: A marked group loses three 1s and the tail gains two groups (walk_down); the walker steps one group left and the tail gains one (walk_left); it merges into the marked group before it (walk_merge); a tail ending in 1^6 becomes a marked item (push). Each for every tail length and every tape further left, in 10q + 23 steps (13 for push).

claims.title: The shallow carry
claims.text: When the last marked group is 1 0 (m = 1) and the tail has q = 4k + r groups, and the item has at least k + 1 groups: the item gives up k + 1 groups and is marked 6 (r < 2) or 3 (r ≥ 2); the tail becomes 5k groups (r < 2) or 5k + 3 (r ≥ 2), ending in 1^6 when r is odd; the sweep takes 50k² + 88k + 28 steps (r < 2) or 50k² + 138k + 82 (r ≥ 2), plus 7 when r is odd. Checked against cell-by-cell sweeps on 1,111 random carries (with 1,023 random walker sweeps and 488 pushes).

claims.title: The hybrid simulator is exact
claims.text: Walker phases are applied at once (x steps left: 2x sweeps, tail +3x, 20qx + 30x(x−1) + 56x steps), shallow carries in closed form, everything else cell by cell. Without phase jumps it reproduces every sweep start of the first 3·107 steps of the direct run (the Python model in py/walker.py does the same for 107 steps); with them it reaches the same configurations at the same steps.

claims.title: No halt in 3.2·10<sup>12</sup> steps
claims.text: The hybrid simulator ran 3.2·10<sup>12</sup> steps without a halt.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: Collatz-like
claims.text: The tail length is multiplied by about 5/4 at each carry and by about 3 at each walker pass; which branch a carry takes depends on q mod 4 and on how much the item before can give. Halting configurations exist among the deep carries (for example the items (0,1) (3,3) (1,1) with a tail of 10 groups halt after 1,164 steps; py/walker.py check runs it), so whether the run ever reaches one is a question about this map.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. A marker walks left across the tape one group at a time, and every group it passes reappears three times at the right end; when the marker is used up it borrows from the group before it with a carry that multiplies the tail by about 5/4. Rules like these, a mix of multiplications and remainders, are how Collatz-like problems look, and this one is no easier.

facts.text: No halt in an exact hybrid simulation.
The walker sweeps are proved in Lean for all lengths.
The arithmetic behind the run, Collatz-like.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.593).
After 109 steps the tape spans 45,722 cells (140 left of the start, 39,740 right), with a density of 1s of 0.667.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: What the tape is made of
html: Cut the tape after every 0: it is a sequence of groups 1^m 0. Almost all of them are 1 1 0; the others are marked, with m = 1, 3, 4, 6 or 7. The tape starts with the marked group 1 0, which never changes, and ends with 1 1 and the head (state C) on the blank cell after it. Write it as items (x, m): x plain groups followed by a marked group 1^m 0, then the tail, q plain groups and 1 1.

sections.heading: The walker
html: Each sweep runs left from the right end to the last marked group and back. If it has m ≥ 4 ones, it loses three and the tail gains two groups; if m = 3, the mark moves one group to the left (m becomes 6) and the tail gains one group; so every two sweeps the walker moves one group left and the tail gains three groups: each group the walker crosses becomes three at the end. When the walker reaches the marked group before it, it merges into it (m + 4) and goes on. Every one of these sweeps takes 10q + 23 steps (Lean: walk_down, walk_left, walk_merge).

sections.heading: The carry: q → 5q/4
html: When the last marked group is 1 0 (m = 1), the sweep becomes a carry: with q = 4k + r tail groups, it takes k + 1 groups from the item before and leaves a tail of 5k groups (r = 0, 1) or 5k + 3 (r = 2, 3), with a new walker mark of 6 or 3 ones; when r is odd the tail becomes a new marked item. If the item before has fewer than k + 1 groups, the carry reaches further left and rearranges several items (a deep carry, simulated cell by cell).

So the run alternates multiplication by 3 (the walker) and by about 5/4 (the carry), with the branch chosen by remainders mod 4 and by whether the item before can pay: a Collatz-like system.

sections.heading: Where it could halt
html: The halting transition is F reading 0. The walker sweeps and shallow carries never reach it (they are exact rules that end in a new sweep). Halting configurations do exist among the deep carries: for example items (0,1) (3,3) (1,1) with a tail of 10 groups halt during the carry. So the question is whether the orbit of this Collatz-like map ever produces such a deep carry; nothing known decides that.

sections.heading: What is proved
html: In Lean (kernel): the four walker sweeps for every tail length (lean/Rules.lean). The carry formulas and the hybrid simulator are trusted computations, checked against direct simulation.

summary: A marker walks left through groups 110, turning each group it passes into three at the right end; when it is used up, a carry turns the tail of q groups into about 5q/4 (q = 4k + r: 5k or 5k + 3), a Collatz-like map; exact hybrid simulation to 3.2e12 steps without a halt.
